question.text: A bag contains six balls of different colours. Two balls are drawn in succession with replacement. The probability that both the balls are of the same colour is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math>. Next four balls are drawn in succession with replacement and the probability that exactly three balls are of the same colours is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>q</mi></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>:</mo><mi>n</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> are co-prime, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></math> is equal to

solution.text:
Given,

A bag contains six balls of different colours, two balls are drawn in succession with replacement,

The probability that both the balls are of the same colour will be p=636

Now Next four balls are drawn in succession with replacement and the probability that exactly three balls are of the same colours is q,

So, probability will be q=C16×C15×C1464=1201296=554

Now the ratio of p & q will be pq=95

Now, on comparing with pq=mn⇒m+n=14
